chunks: And from Yazeed bin Sinan and Uthman bin Abu Shayba, he said: Musa bin Ismaeel narrated to us, he said: Hammad bin Salama narrated to us, from Sammak bin Harb, from Jabir bin Samra, who said: I heard the Prophet saying:
"This Islam will remain strong until twelve caliphs." Then he said a word that I did not understand, so I asked my father: What did he say? He said: He said: All of them are from Quraysh.
ai.seo_question: How many caliphs will there be according to the Prophet's prophecy and which tribe will they belong to?
ai.summary: This hadith, known as the 'Hadith al-Khulafa', is a cornerstone of Shia eschatology, where the twelve caliphs are identified as the Prophet's successors culminating in the twelfth Imam, Muhammad al-Mahdi. While Sunni traditions often view the 'from Quraysh' clause as a condition for legitimacy, Shia scholarship interprets it as a specific descriptor of the twelve Imams' lineage, emphasizing their divine appointment and continuity of authority.
